scientific_summary: Separately, PMID 41056568 provides access-limited acute contractile evidence in 38 older adults given 500 mg quercetin glycoside or placebo before two exercise sessions. The complete original abstract reports greater post-exercise electrically elicited torque decline with active ingestion at low and moderate intensity (P=.014 and .025), with a nonsignificant high-intensity contrast (P=.792); differing subgroup P values do not establish an intensity interaction. The displayed correlation caption supports paired participant-level QUE-minus-PLA change contrasts among contributing participants, while allocation/order, washout and complete paired outcomes for all 38 remain unknown. No native torque magnitudes, confidence intervals, full analysis model or safety findings were recovered. The glycoside label does not establish matching manufacturer or chemistry with the earlier San-Ei preparation. Acute contractile decline may reflect exercise stress; neither chronic benefit nor chronic harm follows. The existing six-week strength positive and separate longer-trial nulls remain intact. Source and independent review read the complete indexed abstract, first-page publisher preview and five displayed captions, not the remaining main or native tables/plots. This bounded refinement adds no MVA, BUBR1, renewal, fidelity or superiority claim and does not change reserve disposition.
integration_precision: The displayed quercetin correlation caption supports participant-level paired QUE-minus-PLA changes for contributors; allocation/order/washout/all-38 complete pairs remain unknown.
